findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in the reports bucket (which is seeded with a vendor roster spreadsheet) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption. Any data written here is at rest without a customer-controlled key boundary.

There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no explicit ACL or bucket policy for this bucket, so nothing prevents a later ACL or policy change from exposing the stored reports and vendor roster publicly.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial export data is stored unencrypted by default rather than under a KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so account- or bucket-level public ACLs/policies are not categorically denied for sensitive ledger data.
Versioning and access logging are configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so model artifacts (and all their versions) are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, leaving it open to accidental exposure via a future ACL or bucket policy change.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration. Operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, procedures and occasionally credentials, and are stored unencrypted here.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, so public ACLs or policies are not structurally blocked.

The audit log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block. Access logs record request sources and object keys across the estate, and nothing here prevents a public ACL or policy from being applied.

force_destroy = true on the audit/log-delivery bucket, combined with the absence of object lock or a restrictive bucket policy, allows the audit evidence and all its versions to be deleted, undermining tamper-resistance of the logging trail.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no server_side_encryption argument into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which itself has no default encryption rule, so this potentially sensitive third-party data is written to S3 in an unencrypted state.
